content: Haiti - News : Zapping... Haiti - Maritime Scholarships : Call for Applications Haiti - Security : The United States lifts restrictions that limited its cooperation with the FAd'H Haiti - Moscow : Haitian student Slanda François, detained in Russia, released Zapping Haiti of July 24, 2026 more news Donation from Brazil of 10,000 doses of human rabies vaccine Haiti's PM pays tribute to the great figures of Konpa FLASH : Medinel Zamor injured, out of the U-20 Champions League Championship Colombia : Haiti's Mission on cocoa Venezuela : Haiti honors its medical brigade returning from its solidarity mission more news Donation from Brazil of 10,000 doses of human rabies vaccine 25/07/2026 11:02:52 On Thursday, July 22, 2026, the Ministry of Public Health received a donation of 10,000 doses of human rabies vaccine at the PROMESS warehouse. The donation was provided by the Government of Brazil through the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO). The delivery of this significant donation to Haiti was made possible through the joint efforts of PANAFTOSA, the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), and the logistical support of the World Food Programme (WFP), which facilitated the air transport of the vaccines to Port-au-Prince. This donation comes at a time when rabies remains a public health threat in Haiti. Between the first and twenty-fourth epidemiological weeks of 2026, 1,481 attacks by animals suspected of having rabies were reported in the country, including 3 deaths, with the situation remaining concentrated in the Central and Western departments. Although this disease is preventable with prompt treatment after exposure, it is almost always fatal once symptoms appear. Access to rabies vaccines is therefore essential to protect populations exposed to animal bites. Thanks to this contribution from the Brazilian Government, health authorities will have a strengthened stockpile, enabling them to improve the care of people exposed to rabies and support prevention efforts in several departments of the country. This initiative illustrates the importance of regional solidarity and coordinated international cooperation in addressing health challenges. It is part of the ongoing efforts of the Ministry of Public Health and Population (MSPP), with the support of friendly countries like Brazil and the United States, and its partners like the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), to reduce the risk of rabies-related deaths and ensure better access to essential health products. content: EAST PROVIDENCE, R.I. (WPRI) — On Friday, July 24, the city of Pawtucket announced that two raccoons tested positive for rabies . Around the same time, the state of Rhode Island disclosed that West Nile virus was detected in a mosquito sample collected in Cranston . In this edition of Beyond the Forecast , 12 News Meteorologist Steven Matregrano goes in-depth on both topics. First, he speaks with Dr. Scott Marshall, Rhode Island’s state veterinarian, about what rabies is, which species it can affect and what to do if you come across a wild animal. Dr. Jannelle Couret, a mosquito abatement coordinator with the R.I. Department of Environmental Management, then joins the show to explain how to reduce the risk of mosquito-borne illnesses and protect yourself against mosquito bites. Locations are not exact and are meant to illustrate findings by community. Source: RI DEM/RI DOH, MA DPH Download the WPRI 12 and Pinpoint Weather 12 apps to get breaking news and weather alerts.
